subject: whether a plain letter under 2-Set Korean still goes out under a layout that types its letter when TIS offers Dvorak as its ASCII-capable layout
question: With Dvorak, on which most of these keys type another letter, made TIS's ASCII-capable layout before every call, does each of the eight plain-letter operations go out under ABC through CGEventChannel alone and change Logic's state under the candidate and not under the control?

reverify.command: python3 Scripts/livekit/live_1039_plain_letters_under_2set_korean.py <worktree> <head> <candidate debug build> <control debug build without the switch> --ascii-history-tool <swiftc build of Scripts/livekit/ax_1039_ascii_history.swift> (run as /usr/bin/python3 under 2-Set Korean, with LPM_LIVE_LOCK naming a held lock and LPM_EVIDENCE_ROOT an absolute directory exported)
reverify.expected: exit 0; every control call refused and moved nothing; every candidate call went out through CGEvent under the layout that types its key's U.S. letter (Dvorak for A, ABC for the other seven letters), moved its reading and moved it back, and 2-Set Korean read back after it
reverify.cost: about three minutes per language on the locale-campaign fixture; needs LIVE.lock, the 2-Set Korean source, and the Accessibility grant for /usr/bin/python3

method: live_1039_plain_letters_under_2set_korean.py ran at 5729fc47 under the 2-Set Korean source in ten languages. Both servers were debug builds started with LOGIC_MCP_DEBUG_ONLY_CHANNEL=CGEvent, and the MIDI key-command approval was withdrawn for the run and put back byte for byte. The candidate was built at ae33818c; the control from the same tree with CGEventChannel.swift as at 07d76426, which has no input-source switch. Before every call, Scripts/livekit/ax_1039_ascii_history.swift enabled the Dvorak layout, selected it and selected 2-Set Korean again, so that TIS's ASCII-capable layout, the one the channel is offered, read as Dvorak; its reading was recorded with each call, and the tool selected ABC and 2-Set Korean and disabled Dvorak at the end. Per language, on a fresh launch of the fixture, the control was called once per operation and the candidate twice per toggle; record was followed by stop and undo. The state was read through Accessibility from the harness process: the control-bar checkbox the canon names for record, cycle, metronome, mixer and library, the one unnamed control-bar checkbox for the piano roll, per-depth role counts for automation, and slider values for zoom to fit. The arrange window was raised and the Tracks header rail focused before every call. Which letters Logic's key command set binds with no modifier was read from its preferences (KeyCommands) in each language. Before the run, this host's key command 474, Toggle Metronome Click, was moved from Control-Shift-R to plain K, the binding Apple's U.S. preset gives it; the preferences were backed up first.
conclusion: 160 of 160 checks passed in 10 languages. The control refused every call and no reading moved. Before every candidate call TIS offered com.apple.keylayout.Dvorak as its ASCII-capable layout; under the candidate every call went out through CGEvent and 2-Set Korean read back after it; nav.zoom_to_fit, transport.record, transport.toggle_cycle, transport.toggle_metronome, view.toggle_library, view.toggle_mixer, view.toggle_piano_roll went out under com.apple.keylayout.ABC; automation.toggle_view went out under com.apple.keylayout.Dvorak in every language, by the layout each reply named; 8 of the 8 operations changed Logic's state and changed it back in every language.
limits: One Logic installation, one fixture, one keyboard input source (2-Set Korean).

This host's key command set was changed for the run: command 474 moved from Control-Shift-R to plain K. With the host's own set, K reaches Logic and runs nothing, and the metronome cannot change by its key.
The piano roll, automation and zoom readings are structural and unnamed; the canon has no label for the editors' checkbox or the automation view.
The waits around the key (100 ms each side) were not varied.
The run was made at 5729fc47; both binaries were built from ae33818c, and the commits between change only the harness, its history tool, its predicate test and records.
Only Dvorak was offered as the other layout; AZERTY and others rest on the unit tests.

canon_not_applicable.reason: This record states what the harness read as booleans, counts and operation ids, and the input-source ids the server reported; it quotes no string Logic ships.
